title: Why plane windows are round
idea: Why airplane windows are round instead of square

lines.text: In 1952, the Comet became the first *jet airliner.*
Jets fly high, so the cabin is *pumped full of air.*
Every flight, the metal skin *stretched and relaxed.*
the stress was up to *three times higher.*
Cracks at the corners *ripped the cabin open.*

scenes.kicker: A round window has no corners,

hooks: Your plane window is round for a *deadly* reason.
One shape *broke* the first jet airliner.
caption: The first jet airliner had square-cornered windows. In 1954 two of them broke apart in the air. Every plane window since has been rounded.

sources.claim: The de Havilland Comet flew its first passenger service on May 2, 1952, with square cabin windows. BOAC Flight 781 (January 10, 1954) and South African Airways Flight 201 (April 8, 1954) broke up in flight. Investigators blamed metal fatigue from repeated pressurising, with cracks starting at the square corners of cutouts
sources.source: Jason Lefkowitz, Why airplane windows have round corners (2016)

sources.claim: The metal around the corners took two to three times more stress than the rest of the cabin. Later aircraft got rounded or oval windows
sources.source: Yahoo News UK, The alarming reason plane windows were changed from square to round

notes: Detail for the pinned comment: the fatal crack is usually traced to the corner of a squarish cutout in the cabin roof, not a passenger window, but the cause is the same. Every picture in this video is a custom animation drawn for it, told by one engineer character who reacts in every scene.
